Article Title: SC seeks Centre, Delhi Police response to plea challenging Jantar Mantar’s de-notification as protest site

SC seeks response on Jantar Mantar losing protest site status

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday sought responses from the Centre, Delhi government and Delhi Police on a plea challenging the de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site.Earlier this week, the ministry of home affairs de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site and identified three alternative venues for demonstrations: Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground.In a notice issued by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, the police said the Ministry of Home Affairs had constituted a committee to examine suitable alternative venues where citizens could exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations. The decision was taken based on the committee’s recommendations.The decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar came against the backdrop of the Cockroach Janta Party’s planned demonstration on October 10.However, a Centre-led crackdown largely curtailed the protest, with over 7,000 people detained, including several political leaders.The Centre also deployed 35,000 security personnel and imposed restrictions on metro services and internet access.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought responses from the Centre, Delhi government and Delhi Police on a plea challenging the de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Earlier this week, the ministry of home affairs had identified three alternative venues for demonstrations: Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground.

Article Title: Leh Apex Body condemns Chinese government over Ladakh remarks
Article Text:
Leh Apex Body rejects China govt remarks on Ladakh

SRINAGAR: The Leh Apex Body (LAB) a major political and religious grouping of the Ladakh region today condemned China’s remarks on Ladakh stating that Ladakh has never been China’s part in recorded history and Ladakh is an integral part of India.“We are holding this press conference to condemn the recent comments made by a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson about Ladakh. The spokesperson claimed that western Ladakh has always been part of China. We categorically reject this statement. Ladakh has never been under Chinese control and there is no such reference in recorded history,” Chering Dorjay Lakrook, LAB co-chairman said addressing a press conference. LAB member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk and others were also present during the presser.“We strongly condemn these statements and appeal to the Government of India, particularly the Union Home Ministry, to condemn such remarks in the strongest possible terms and send a clear message to the Chinese government that we are not prepared to give up even an inch of Ladakh, including Aksai Chin , which is under China’s illegal occupation but has historically been part of Ladakh,” Lakrook said.“We expect China to exercise caution and think carefully before making such statements. For the past 75 years, the people of Ladakh have been happily living as part of India,” Lakrook said.On Tuesday China opposed India's decision to assign standardised names to 28 strategic locations and geographical features in Ladakh. China claimed that the areas belonged to it. "China has never recognised the so-called ‘Union Territory of Ladakh’ unilaterally and illegally established by India," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a media briefing in Beijing.Konchok Stanzin, former Councillor of Chushul region in the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council Leh, said, “We condemn the statement made by the Chinese spokesperson about Ladakh because Ladakh is an integral part of India. Those of us living along the border including the younger generations, have stood with the Indian Army to defend our territory. During the 1962 war with China, civilians in the border areas also fought to protect our land. ”“We reject and condemn the comments made by China about Ladakh. The Chinese government must think carefully before making such statements and the Government of India must strongly reject such statements. We want to remain with India as we have always done and we have consistently resisted Chinese aggression,” he said.“On behalf of the people living along the border, I want to reiterate that these statements are not in the interests of Ladakh and they are entirely condemnable. We strongly condemn them,” he added.Deldan Namgyal former MLA Nubra said since 1962, the people of Ladakh have stood against China to protect their territory. “I also want to make one thing clear the people of Ladakh share a spiritual bond with His Holiness the Dalai Lama, who was forced to leave Tibet.”“No one, whether in India or elsewhere, should assume that the people of Ladakh are agents of China. We have a spiritual enmity with China. We will always stand with India and continue to defend this sacred land,” he added.“I appeal to the Government of India to condemn the Chinese statement at the highest level and in the strongest possible terms. Thank you.”Meanwhile, the crucial round of sub-committee level talks between Ladakh leaders and ministry of home affairs (MHA) officials will be held in Leh Thursday afternoon.The sub-committee level meeting, scheduled for 4 pm, will be attended by leaders of LAB Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), Ladakh MP Haji Haneefa Jan and ministry officials.
Article Summary: The Leh Apex Body (LAB) a major political and religious grouping of the Ladakh region today condemned China’s remarks on Ladakh. “We strongly condemn these statements and appeal to the Government of India, particularly the Union Home Ministry, to condemn such remarks in the strongest possible terms,” said LAB co- chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook.

Article Title: Dhami government took steps at every level in Ankita Bhandari case: U'khand BJP chief

Dhami government took steps at every level in Ankita Bhandari case: U'khand BJP chief

Uttarakhand BJP chief Mahendra Bhatt on Wednesday said the state took steps at every stage in the Ankita Bhandari case and ensured an impartial investigation.Bhatt said the Pushkar Dhami government treated the murder case with seriousness and ensured the accused were arrested right after the crime was unravelled.He said the government also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) and made arrangements for prosecution and addressing the family's demands.The remarks of the Rajya Sabha MP came against the backdrop of a protest at India Gate in the national capital by Bhandari's parents, who were joined in their demand for justice by Rahul Gandhi, the Lok Sabha leader of the opposition.Bhandari, an employee at a resort in Uttarakhand, was murdered in September 2022.Bhatt dismissed the Congress's allegation that the probe into the receptionist's killing was laced with malice."Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami made it clear from the outset that the safety of women and strict action against criminals are the government's top priorities. Accordingly, instructions were issued to the police for immediate action. The accused were arrested and sent to jail within 24 hours of the incident coming to light," he said.A chargesheet was submitted to the court based on evidence and witness testimonies, and the "prosecution effectively argued the case in court," he said."Through the judicial process, the guilty were sentenced to life imprisonment; this verdict was delivered based on the evidence presented and established legal procedures," Bhatt said.The BJP leader said the Dhami government also acceded to Bhandari's parents' demand for a CBI probe, and that they were given Rs 25 lakh in financial support."The issue of securing justice for Ankita Bhandari extends beyond a mere criminal case; it is also linked to women's safety, sensitive governance, and public trust in the legal system," he added. Article Title: 'Consistently sides with those who exploit women': BJP targets Congress over Akoijam's dismissal from JNU
Article Text:
Prof Angomcha Bimol Akoijam.

NEW DELHI: BJP on Thursday attacked Congress over dismissal of its Inner Manipur MP, Angomcha Bimol Akoijam from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) following an internal inquiry into sexual harassment allegations by female students.Addressing reporters, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj accused the Congress leadership of remaining silent on the issue and alleged that the party was siding with those accused of exploiting women.“It is highly unfortunate that the Congress party consistently sides with those who exploit women. When Bimal Akoijam, a sitting MP from the Congress party, sexually harassed 11 female students, JNU’s internal committee found that the complaints filed by these students against him were truthful and substantiated by facts. Consequently, on October 9, 2026, Bimal Akoijam was dismissed from his position at JNU,” the BJP MP said.“Yet, there is an absolutely deafening silence from Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, Kharge ji, and Sonia Gandhi... Today, under the guidance and leadership of our Mahila Morcha National President and fellow MP, Rupkumari Choudhary, we met with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Om Birla.... We appealed to the President, Droupadi Murmu.Yesterday, a delegation met with the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women (NCW), Vijaya Rahatkar, and today, we submitted a memorandum to Om Birla. We had a very productive discussion...” she added.Earlier on Wednesday, Delhi Police has served a notice to Akoijam, asking him to join an investigation into the allegations. The notice comes days after police registered an FIR following a complaint forwarded by JNU’s chief security officer for necessary legal action, news agency PTI reported.The documents submitted to the police included the university’s dismissal order, the internal committee’s inquiry report and its assessment of the allegations.The FIR invokes provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to sexual harassment and words, gestures or acts intended to insult a woman’s modesty. Police documents refer to an incident on May 6 and an unspecified period before that date.Akoijam, a professor at JNU’s Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences, was dismissed with immediate effect on October 9 following an internal inquiry.According to reports, several female students filed sexual harassment complaints against Akoijam in May. The allegations included claims that he invited students to his campus residence under the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to sexually harass them. Some students also alleged that he made inappropriate remarks in class.Akoijam has denied the allegations, describing the complaints as politically motivated. He has also challenged the university’s account of the inquiry process.
Article Summary: BJP attacks Congress over dismissal of its Inner Manipur MP, Angomcha Bimol Akoijam from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) following an internal inquiry into sexual harassment allegations by female students. Delhi Police has served a notice to A Koijam, asking him to join an investigation into the allegations.

Article Title: Over 150 more 'Aam Aadmi Clinics' opened in Punjab: CM Bhagwant Mann
Article Text:
Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann

Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday dedicated 154 new 'Aam Aadmi Clinics' to the people, taking the total to 1,244 in the state.Mann asserted that his government's priority is to deliver quality healthcare, education and employment rather than indulge in "politics of slogans".Addressing a public gathering at village Harkhowal in Chabbewal here, he highlighted over 6.48 crore OPD visits at the Clinics and healthcare coverage worth up to Rs 10 lakh for 54.20 lakh families, while warning that a change of government could put public welfare initiatives, including free bus travel for women and monthly financial assistance, at risk.Assembly elections in Punjab are scheduled to be held early next year.Launching a sharp attack on AAP rivals, Mann said that they want to shut down Aam Aadmi Clinics, the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna, Rs 1,000 monthly assistance for women and free bus travel, as they cannot digest the people-centric initiatives being implemented by his government.Highlighting that the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna covers 54.20 lakh families and nearly 8 lakh beneficiaries have received treatment, he reiterated that his government's priorities are people's healthcare, children's education and youth employment, not slogan-driven politics.Mann said today, 154 new Aam Aadmi Clinics have been dedicated to the people of Punjab.With this, the total number of these Clinics in Punjab has reached 1,244.He alleged that successive governments which ruled Punjab only looted the state.Hitting out at rival parties, Mann said, "they may resort to any number of malicious tactics to defame us, but as long as I have the love and trust of the people, I have nothing to fear from them"."The historic mandate given by the people of Punjab has placed a tremendous responsibility on our shoulders, and we are fulfilling our promises through concrete action. The difference between the previous governments and our government is clear."Earlier, power was treated as a means to benefit some families and select individuals, but today, governance revolves around the common people, their aspirations and their welfare. The winds of development are blowing across Punjab, and no conspiracy by the opposition can stop this transformation," he said.Launching a sharp attack on the opposition, he said that parties which had governed Punjab for decades were now struggling with internal divisions, a lack of credible leadership and an inability to present a constructive vision for the state.Taking a dig at the Shiromani Akali Dal, Mann said, "The Akali Dal once claimed that it would govern Punjab for 25 years, but today it is struggling to maintain its political relevance..."Criticising the Congress, he said, "Congress leaders are unable to present a united front even on matters concerning Punjab's future. Those who ruled Punjab for years and failed to fulfil the aspirations of its people are now unable to tolerate the work being done by AAP government.They are joining hands against us because they have no credible agenda for Punjab, but the people of the state continue to stand firmly with us." Mann said that the people of Punjab had rejected the politics of corruption, nepotism and personal enrichment and were now demanding accountable governance and tangible results."The previous Akali governments failed to protect Punjab's youth from the drug menace, while the sacrilege incidents inflicted a severe blow on the party's credibility among the people. The opposition must understand that people have rejected the politics of corruption, nepotism and personal enrichment.I appeal to the people to remain vigilant against attempts to mislead them. The trust and blessings of the people are our greatest political strength," he said.Meanwhile, of the 154 more Aam Aadmi Clinics dedicated to the people of Punjab on Wednesday include 36 in Amritsar, 26 in Patiala, 17 in Ludhiana, 12 in Gurdaspur, 11 in Jalandhar and 10 in SAS Nagar (Mohali).Mann reiterated that the expansion of Aam Aadmi Clinics, free medicines and diagnostic tests, and the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna were part of the state government's broader commitment to ensuring accessible and affordable healthcare for the people of Punjab.
Article Summary: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday dedicated 154 new 'Aam Aadmi Clinics' to the people. The total number of these Clinics in Punjab has reached 1,244. Mann said his government's priority is to deliver quality healthcare, education and employment rather than indulge in "politics of slogans"

Article Title: 'Nobody can browbeat judiciary': SC issues notice to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others over October 12 march
Article Text:
File photo: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi stands next to Priyanka Gandhi as opposition parties marched to SC to file plea against SIR

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi , Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other INDIA bloc leaders on a plea challenging their October 12 march to the apex court over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.During the hearing, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said, “We are not sitting in ivory towers,” after lawyers referred to attempts to “browbeat” the judiciary through the march. The CJI said the court would ask Rahul to explain how crowds entered the Supreme Court premises during the demonstration.The INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli – March for Democracy’, led by Rahul, brought thousands of supporters into central Delhi on October 12. The opposition was demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the SIR exercise over alleged electoral irregularities.The march saw supporters gather along roads between Connaught Place and the Supreme Court, waving party flags and raising slogans. Police stopped the procession near Barakhamba Road, where some demonstrators pushed through barricades as security personnel attempted to hold them back.The crowd later gathered along Bhagwan Das Road, with some supporters climbing onto parked police vehicles and buses.Rahul was joined by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Yadav, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav and other INDIA bloc leaders. The procession followed the CJI’s refusal to meet opposition representatives seeking to submit a memorandum on alleged electoral irregularities.He had advised them to file a formal petition, citing matters already pending before the court.The opposition’s separate petition challenging the SIR process alleges arbitrary voter deletions and seeks greater transparency and safeguards in the revision of electoral rolls. The Supreme Court also issued notice to the Election Commission of India on that plea.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders on a plea challenging their October 12 march. The opposition was demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the SIR exercise over alleged electoral irregularities.

Article Title: ACP Vivek Bhagat case: HC refuses urgent hearing on woman journalist’s arrest protection plea
Article Text:
​Delhi HC defers journalist’s arrest protection plea

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high ourt on Thursday declined to urgently list a woman journalist’s plea seeking interim protection from arrest in a case registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act on a complaint by Delhi Police ACP Vivek Bhagat.The court said it would hear the matter on Friday.The plea was mentioned before a division bench of acting chief justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and justice Sanjay Sharma. The journalist’s counsel sought an urgent hearing on Thursday and requested interim protection from arrest, but the bench declined to take up the matter immediately.The FIR was registered at Parliament Street police station following a complaint by Bhagat over alleged caste-based humiliation, intimidation and obstruction of official duty during a protest at Buta Singh Roundabout on October 3.According to the FIR, Bhagat, who is posted in the Connaught Place subdivision of New Delhi district, was deployed for law-and-order duty during a protest against the Election Commission of India when the alleged incident took place. He claimed that a journalist made derogatory remarks about his caste identity while referring to his nameplate and appointment as an assistant commissioner of police.Bhagat stated in his complaint that he belongs to the Scheduled Caste community.The FIR names Rosy, Gajendra and an unidentified person as accused.The journalist, meanwhile, has accused Bhagat of sexual harassment in connection with the October 3 incident. Her allegations and the claims made in the FIR remain subject to investigation and judicial determination.The FIR invokes Sections 221, 356(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 3(1)(p), 3(1)(q), 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The High Court is scheduled to hear the journalist’s plea for interim protection from arrest on Friday.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court declines to urgently list a woman journalist’s plea seeking interim protection from arrest. The case was registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act on a complaint by Delhi Police ACP Vivek Bhagat. The court said it would hear the matter on Friday.

Article Title: 'White supremacist views': US teen held with rifle, ammo over Hindu temple attack plot
Article Text:
US teen arrested over alleged mass shooting plot targeting Hindu temple

Police in Palatine, Illinois, arrested a 19-year-old man following an investigation into threats of a potential mass shooting at a Hindu temple.The investigation began on October 11, when the Palatine Police Department received information from the Mount Prospect Police Department about concerning electronic communications allegedly sent by Alexandros Paporakis.Investigators said Paporakis had shared a document outlining an alleged plan for a mass shooting at the Hindu temple. He also shared images of a rifle, magazines, body armour and other tactical gear and accessories.FBI investigators examined electronic communications and a document attributed to Paporakis titled “Why I Fought: A K A: (Aurora Shooter’s Manifesto).” The document contained white supremacist and extremist views, including references to violence against people of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian descent.Detectives believe Paporakis may have been planning an attack on October 11, possibly targeting a Hindu place of worship in the Aurora area. Police subsequently contacted Hindu places of worship within their jurisdiction to alert them to the threat.Paporakis was charged with one count of making a terrorist threat, a Class X felony, and one count of unlawful possession of weapons. He appeared for a detention hearing on Wednesday, where a judge ordered him to remain in custody."The seriousness of this alleged threat cannot be overstated. Through the immediate sharing of information and coordinated response by the Palatine and Mount Prospect Police Departments, officers were able to identify and take the suspect into custody. We are grateful for the FBI’s assistance in the subsequent investigation and commend the individual who initially came forward with this information. Protecting our communities and places of worship remains a priority, and we will continue working with our law enforcement partners as this investigation moves forward," Palatine Police Chief William Nord said, as cited by ANI.Paporakis was arrested as he was leaving his residence. During a subsequent search of his home, Palatine Police detectives recovered a rifle, multiple loaded magazines, hundreds of rounds of additional ammunition, tactical gear and other items believed to be relevant to the investigation.The recovered items included a tactical vest with body armour and a patch bearing imagery associated with white supremacist extremism.
Article Summary: Police in Palatine, Illinois, arrested a 19-year-old man following an investigation into threats of a potential mass shooting at a Hindu temple. Alexandros Paporakis had shared a document outlining an alleged plan for a mass shooting. He also shared images of a rifle, magazines, body armour and other tactical gear and accessories.

Article Title: ‘Stop protecting the VIP’: Ankita Bhandari's parents detained after overnight protest over governor appointment
Article Text:
Congress backs parents as Delhi Police break up overnight dharna

After an overnight vigil at India Gate, a pre-dawn swoop by Delhi Police brought the dharna for “Justice to Ankita Bhandari” to an end. The cops arrived at the protest site at 4 am and took away the wailing parents of Ankita Bhandari, who was murdered in Uttarakhand in 2022.Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and, later, AICC general secretary KC Venugopal visited the protest site on Wednesday evening to express solidarity with the parents. After they left, scores of Congress MPs, MLAs and workers of the Youth Congress and NSUI, among others, joined the dharna. Uttarakhand MLA and Congress office-bearer Qazi Nizamuddin, MPs Pawan Khera, Jothi Mani and Imran Pratapgarhi, Congress spokespersons Supriya Shrinate, Gurdeep Sappal and Ragini Nayak, Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib, NSUI president Vinod Jakhar and Mahila Congress president Alka Lamba, among others, joined the vigil, which continued until early morning before being disrupted by the cops.Videos of the police action went viral, with Chib, Jakhar and others even trying to intercept the bus carrying the detainees.Ankita’s parents arrived from Uttarakhand on Wednesday evening and sat on a dharna along with activist Yogita Bhayana, holding a placard that read, “Stop protecting the VIP”. The continuing controversy over Ankita’s murder received a fresh lease of life with the appointment of BJP leader Dushyant Gautam as governor.The controversy revolves around the “VIP” who had allegedly sought “special service” at the infamous resort then owned by the son of a BJP leader. Ankita resisted the pressure. Her body was found in a canal in 2022, leading to a murder case.In a social media post, the Congress said there were allegations that Gautam was the “VIP” in question. “Narendra Modi has rewarded Gautam with the governorship of Sikkim. The girls and women of the country are watching how Modi and his govt are protecting Gautam.Instead of giving them justice, the entire BJP govt is hellbent on suppressing the voice of Ankita’s parents,” it said.Ankita’s father urged the President of India to put Gautam’s appointment as governor on hold until the CBI inquiry into the issue is completed.Ankita’s parents were taken by the cops to Tilak Marg police station, where they were swiftly joined by Congress leaders protesting the police action against the parents, who were seeking justice for their deceased daughter.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and AICC general secretary KC Venugopal visited the protest site on Wednesday evening. Scores of Congress MPs, MLAs and workers of the Youth Congress and NSUI, among others, joined the dharna.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar breach: Das, Ranka sent to 5-day custody
Article Text:
‘Concerns they were likely to breach peace’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: CJP members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been sent to five days of judicial custody, while Ajinkya Shinde has been bound down, after 14 party members allegedly trespassed into Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructed cops on duty. Bound down means an individual has to appear before an IO whenever called and inform cops before leaving the city.Police said the action was prompted by repeated alleged violations of law and concerns that accused could again disturb public peace.Police also feared that they could instigate others. Two FIRs have been registered, including one under the section relating to criminal conspiracy.DCP (New Delhi) Sachin Sharma said, “Police personnel deployed at the spot intervened and attempted to stop them. However, the protesters allegedly obstructed police personnel in the discharge of their official duties.” Subsequently, all the persons were bound down in the respective case as per law.The DCP said that in view of their alleged repeated attempts to disturb peace and violate the law, Ranka, Das, and Shinde were arrested under relevant preventive provisions.“Their alleged attempts to instigate others via social media to engage in similar unlawful activities were also taken into consideration,” he added.The three were produced before the special executive magistrate, where proceedings under Sections 126 (security for keeping peace in other cases) and 170 (arrest to prevent commission of cognisable offences) of the BNSS were initiated. Police also submitted videos of CJP representatives jumping a gate and unfurling the flag at Jantar Mantar Tuesday. The court, considering the kalandra (preventive legal measure) details, in view of their repeated violations of law and serious apprehension that if released on bail, they will again violate law and instigate others, remanded Das and Ranka to five days of judicial custody. Special executive magistrate Mahesh Kumar Meena held that their conduct after being released earlier after executing personal and surety bonds of Rs 50,000 each for maintaining peace and good behaviour showed they were likely to breach “peace and tranquillity”. The magistrate had directed them to “keep peace in the area for a period of one year from the date of order”. Their lawyer, Abhisht Hela, argued that an executive magistrate had no power to order judicial custody and said he would approach Delhi High Court.Shinde was released on personal bond and surety of Rs 5,000. However, he was “bound down to maintain peace and good behaviour for six months”. Under Section 141 of BNSS, a magistrate can order the arrest and detention of a person found to have breached a peace bond executed under Section 136 for the remainder of the bond period. The matter has been listed for further inquiry on Oct 19.The FIR invokes sections 223, which deals with disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant, 332 (house-trespass in order to commit an offence) and 61 (2) (criminal conspiracy) of BNS at Connaught Place police station.The second FIR was registered under sections 221 (obstructing public servant in discharge of his public functions), 115 (voluntarily causing hurt), 132 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty), 121 (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty) and 3 (5) (common intention) of BNS at Parliament Street police station.
Article Summary: CJP members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been sent to five days of judicial custody. Ajinkya Shinde has been bound down, after 14 party members allegedly trespassed into Jantar Mantar. Police said the action was prompted by repeated alleged violations of law.

NEW DELHI: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee is facing two separate legal proceedings in Delhi. A fresh defamation suit has been filed against him at the Saket court over a video allegedly claiming that Lord Ram and Goddess Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile.Separately, Rathee has been served fresh summons in a 2018 criminal defamation case filed by BJP IT Cell member Vikas Pandey over a video titled "BJP IT Cell Part 2".Supreme Court Advocate-on-Record Amita Sachdeva and other petitioners had approached the Delhi high court over the video titled “Can Hindus Eat BEEF? and prayed before the court to issue directions granting an interim restraint on Rathee from creating, uploading, or publishing similar content."Some time ago, Dhruv Rathee published a video claiming that Lord Shri Ram and Mother Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile. We took the matter regarding that video to the Delhi High Court, and the Delhi High Court directed the Govt of India to have the video removed.""On July 15, 2026, the Govt of India directed YouTube to take down the video, after which that petition was disposed of. Following the disposal of the petition, someone extracted a three-minute segment from that 21-minute video and re-uploaded it,” she added.According to Sachdeva, the petitioners approached the Delhi High Court again, which granted them liberty to initiate fresh legal proceedings against Rathee."We approached the Delhi High Court again. The Court granted us the liberty to file a fresh petition or suit against Dhruv Rathee and seek appropriate relief. Acting on that liberty, we filed a suit today in the Saket Court, before the Learned District Judge, seeking a declaration, an injunction, and damages for defamation; the matter was listed for hearing today," she said.Sachdeva said the petitioner's senior counsel, Makarand Natkar, appeared through video conferencing but could not complete his submissions because of technical difficulties. The court subsequently adjourned the matter to November 5."Today, my senior counsel, Makarand Natkar, presented his submissions. He appeared via video conferencing (VC), but due to some technical issues with the VC connection, the submissions could not be completed. Consequently, the Learned District Judge adjourned the matter to November 5, when we will present our fresh submissions," she added.The complainants, who identified themselves as Hindu devotees, alleged that the video hurt their religious sentiments. The suit also seeks an ex-parte ad-interim injunction restraining Google from restoring, hosting, uploading, sharing or disseminating the video, or any video identical or similar in content, after notice and verification of the URL, during the pendency of the suit.Separately, a Delhi court has issued fresh summons to Rathee in a defamation case filed by BJP IT Cell member Vikas Pandey in 2018. The court noted that attempts to serve Rathee had continued for several years.Judicial Magistrate Rahul Jain was hearing Pandey's plea seeking fresh summons. In an order dated October 12, the court said, "From the available record, it is clear that the complainant has been trying to serve the accused no. 1 (Rathee) since the last several years..."Appearing for Pandey, advocate Samaksh Sharma submitted that Rathee ordinarily resides in Austria and had come to India for the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. He argued that fresh summons were necessary to ensure prompt steps could be taken to serve the accused.The court permitted fresh summons to be served through dasti service, allowing the complainant to accompany the process server. Rathee has since been physically served at his Gurugram residence. The proceedings had remained pending amid unsuccessful attempts to serve him since 2019.Speaking about the notice served on Rathee, Pandey said, "The court summons has been pasted outside Dhruv Rathee's home because he was not coming out. This stems from eight years ago when Dhruv Rathee created around three videos alleging that I offered Rs 50 lakh to someone to spread fake news against him.”“When Arvind Kejriwal amplified this fake news by tweeting and retweeting it, I filed a case against both Kejriwal and Dhruv Rathee. While Arvind Kejriwal offered an apology, Dhruv Rathee never appeared before the court. Consequently, a notice and summons were issued, which my lawyer pasted outside his Gurugram home..." he added.The case also reached the Supreme Court in connection with a retweet of the video by Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal. In February 2024, Kejriwal told the apex court that he had made a mistake by retweeting it.The cases come days after Delhi and Gurugram Police detained Rathee at his Sector 56 residence in Gurugram on October 10, ahead of his planned participation in a CJP protest at Jantar Mantar. He was released after around 22 hours.The detention took place amid protests in Delhi led by the CJP, which has been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protests saw extensive security arrangements, barricading, traffic restrictions and the detention of protesters.
Article Summary: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee is facing two separate legal proceedings in Delhi. Article Title: After Musk’s Ambani meltdown, Rubio to visit Reliance refinery

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel next week to Mumbai and Gujarat’s refinery hub Jamnagar, announced the State Department. The brief stopover in Jamnagar, which will see him touring the Reliance oil refinery, is being seen through the lens of Reliance’s plans to invest in a major refinery in Texas, the first of its kind in 50 years in the US and a major priority for the Trump administration.The announcement about Rubio’s Jamnagar visit came days after billionaire Elon Musk’s social media jab – addressing Mukesh Ambani as PM Ambani and the real boss of India – over alleged regulatory delays being faced by the Musk-controlled satellite internet service provider Starlink.This will be Rubio’s second visit to India this year, following his trip to Delhi in May for a meeting of the Quad foreign ministers. Energy is likely to be a key focus area for Rubio during his visit beginning Monday.“He will meet with senior government officials to strengthen the US-India strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation. Secretary Rubio will also meet with business leaders to promote opportunities for commercial investment and economic cooperation,” said the State Department in its announcement.Rubio is also expected to have a bilateral meeting with his counterpart S Jaishankar in Mumbai. The visit comes shortly after another round of tensions over the talent mobility issue, with the US suspending firms, including many from India, from the PERM green card programme. India had strongly condemned remarks by US Vice President J D Vance, who characterized foreign tech workers as foreign indentured servants, calling the statement deeply offensive and unjustified.India had responded angrily to Vice President J D Vance’s remarks describing tech professionals from abroad as foreign indentured servants, calling his remarks deeply offensive and unwarranted.India is also likely to bring up its concerns related to the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA) that empowers the president to impose up to 100 percent tariffs on countries importing Russian oil. That threat may have subsided for now though with the US itself allowing Russia to temporarily export diesel to America and global marketplace. India is expected to reiterate its position that energy security and stable markets must take precedence over rigid geopolitics.Rubio’s visit will also mark the beginning of several high-level engagements between the 2 sides in the next few months. The ministers will meet again on the margins of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta on October 30-31. Another meeting of the Quad foreign ministers will also take place on the sidelines.PM Narendra Modi will also travel to Florida for the G20 summit in Florida on December 14-15. He is expected to have a bilateral meeting with Trump. There’s also the possibility of a Quad leaders’ summit taking place during Modi’s US visit.While the foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta would be the 4th such meeting since the return of Trump to the White House, a leaders’ summit remains elusive. During his visit to India in May, Rubio had described Quad as linchpin and a cornerstone of the US global strategy as a nation. However, there has been no word so far on the dates and likely venue for the next leaders’ summit.
Article Summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel next week to Mumbai and Gujarat’s refinery hub Jamnagar. Rubio will meet with senior government officials to strengthen the US-India strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global dynamics. He will also meet with business leaders to promote opportunities for commercial investment and economic cooperation.

Article Title: ATC software glitch behind Air India false hijack scare? Probe on
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A false hijack alert created a real scare for security agencies and the 306 people on board Air India’s Frankfurt-Delhi flight on Wednesday, with the Boeing 787 getting diverted to Jaipur as a result where everyone had to wait for hours before they could fly to their destination. It is reliably learnt pilots operating the flight, AI 2030, did not squawk the code 7500 used to convey a hijack or unlawful interference, which has to be punched on a keypad like four letter code to unlock phones.Still the recently installed air traffic control radar system at Mumbai, which is now an enroute ATC due to longer routes taken by Indian aircraft flying between Delhi and the west, somehow conveyed that scary message for the erstwhile Vistara B787-9 (VT-TSE). “Once that happened, Mumbai ATC spoke to the pilots who reported that all operations were normal on the flight. But protocols have to be followed in situations like this and so the plane was asked to divert,” said people in the know.Why the false scare happened is now the subject of a probe by both aviation and security agencies, with Mumbai ATC’s new systems being looked at closely. Incidentally, air traffic control has been headless as Airport Authority of India’s position of member (air navigation services) has been vacant for some time now and AAI itself does not have a regular chairman.It remains to be seen how headless AAI’s headless ANS tackles the issue of reportedly false scares that have such an impact on passengers, crew members, security agencies and airline schedules apart from added costs.On landing in Jaipur around 11 am, the plane was parked on a remote bay. For about two hours everyone remained on board before being asked to alight so that security agencies could check them all, the baggage and aircraft before clearing it to take off for Delhi after 2.30 pm with the same set of crew.Senior B787 pilots say there is a “one in a trillion” chance of the code being set to 7500 on the aircraft inadvertently or due to some error. “Each digit has to be physically entered. There is no button that can be inadvertently pressed. So from the pilot or plane side some error to happen is highly remote,” they say.Senior air traffic controllers say Mumbai ATC has a new system. When a pilot squawks 7500 (hijack), then the colour of this aircraft’s dot on the radar screen turns red and an alarm goes off.In a statement, Air India said: “Air India flight AI2030 operating from Frankfurt to Delhi on Oct 14 was diverted to Jaipur following a perceived security concern. The aircraft landed safely in Jaipur. The relevant security agencies carried out the necessary checks and have cleared the aircraft and crew. All passengers disembarked, underwent security checks, and have since reboarded the aircraft. The flight is expected to continue its journey to Delhi shortly.“Air India teams worked proactively with authorities to minimise passenger inconvenience. We sincerely regret the inconvenience caused to our passengers due to this unforeseen disruption and appreciate their patience and understanding. The safety and security of our passengers and crew remain Air India's highest priority,” AI statement added.
Article Summary: Pilots operating the flight, AI 2030, did not squawk the code 7500 used to convey a hijack or unlawful interference. Mumbai ATC spoke to the pilots who reported that all operations were normal on the flight. But protocols have to be followed in situations like this and so the plane was asked to divert.

Article Title: Ankita Bhandari case: 'VIP' question brings her parents to India Gate; Uttarakhand government reacts

Why is the VIP angle still under investigation?

What happened to Ankita Bhandari?

NEW DELHI: Nearly four years after the murder of 19-year-old Ankita Bhandari in Uttarakhand, questions over an alleged VIP’s role in the case have resurfaced following a controversial political appointment.The appointment of former BJP national general secretary Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim governor on Monday has prompted fresh outrage from Ankita’s family, who have named him as the alleged VIP in the case. Her parents are now protesting at India Gate in Delhi, demanding that President Droupadi Murmu halt his appointment until the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) completes its probe into the alleged VIP angle.“Dushyant Kumar should be behind bars... I earnestly request the Honorable President not to appoint Dushyant Kumar as governor until the CBI investigation is concluded,” Ankita’s father, Virendra Singh Bhandari, said in Delhi.Her mother, Soni Devi, said the family was deeply hurt by the appointment and appealed to the President to intervene.“We were deeply pained when we heard the news on the 12th that he (BJP leader Dushyant Kumar Gautam) has now been named Governor.I appeal to the Honourable President, who is herself a woman and will surely understand my sentiments, to halt the move to appoint this individual as Governor until the CBI investigation against him is concluded,” she said.The appointment has triggered fresh political backlash, with the Congress accusing the Modi government of protecting Gautam instead of ensuring justice for Ankita’s family. The allegations against Gautam have not been established in court.The Uttarakhand government on Wednesday said its legal efforts had ensured that the accused in the Ankita Bhandari murder case remained behind bars, after a court once again rejected their bail applications. It cited the life sentences awarded to the convicts, the constitution of a Special Investigation Team (SIT) and the CBI probe ordered at the request of Ankita’s parents as steps taken to secure justice.The government said the accused were arrested within 24 hours of the incident coming to light, while a chargesheet of around 500 pages was prepared, incorporating evidence and statements from nearly 100 witnesses. It also said the prosecution had consistently opposed bail, ensuring the accused remained in custody during the trial. The case ultimately resulted in life imprisonment for the convicts.The state said it had changed the government counsel three times in response to the family’s demands and ordered a CBI investigation after Ankita’s parents sought one. It added that the family received financial assistance of Rs 25 lakh, while jobs were provided to Ankita’s father and brother.The government also criticised Congress leaders and other organisations for repeatedly raising questions over the alleged VIP angle. It said anyone with concrete evidence should present it to the investigating agencies or the court, rather than making public allegations. The government accused political leaders of attempting to politicise the case and mislead the public.Congress MP Pawan Khera questioned why Gautam had been appointed governor before the CBI investigation was completed. He alleged that the decision amounted to granting protection to a person facing allegations.“You granted them immunity. You aren't even waiting for the CBI inquiry. What is the pressure to wrap this up so quickly? Who are you shielding? Is there anyone else you need to protect? Who is being blackmailed here—forcing you to appoint someone as a high-ranking official just to grant them immunity? Why risk everything?” Khera said.He accused the government of siding with the person facing allegations rather than the victim’s family.“The very people who are supposed to deliver justice are not standing with the victim. They have sided with the accused—the person facing the allegations...” he said.In a separate statement, the Congress alleged that Ankita was pressured to provide sexual favours to Gautam and was murdered after refusing. The party accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of rewarding Gautam by appointing him governor."Narendra Modi has rewarded the very Dushyant Gautam against whom allegations were made by appointing him as the Governor of Sikkim. The daughters and women of the country are watching how Narendra Modi and his government are protecting Dushyant Gautam. Instead of delivering justice to Ankita Bhandari, the entire BJP government is bent on silencing the voice of the victim's family," it said.Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also met Ankita’s family at India Gate. Rahul had earlier raised questions over the handling of the case, saying the family was still waiting for justice nearly four years after her death.An FIR was registered against an unidentified VIP in January 2026, following allegations and the circulation of audio and video clips referring to the alleged involvement of a VIP in Ankita’s murder.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami recommended a CBI probe on January 9. The agency subsequently took up the case through its Special Crime Branch and obtained records, including the police FIR and the Special Investigation Team’s report.The investigation has drawn criticism from the Congress. Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee president Ganesh Godiyal alleged that the CBI had made no meaningful progress and had not registered an FIR against the person named by Ankita’s parents. He also announced a one-hour silent fast in Dehradun to protest Gautam’s appointment.The family’s demand is that the alleged VIP angle be investigated and that the appointment be halted until the probe is complete. The allegations against Gautam remain unproven.Ankita, 19, worked as a receptionist at Vanantra Resort near Rishikesh. She was murdered in September 2022, and her body was recovered from the Cheela canal on September 24.The case involved allegations that she was pressured to provide sexual favours to guests at the resort, which was run by Pulkit Arya, the son of a former BJP leader.Resort owner Pulkit Arya, manager Saurabh Bhaskar and another accused, Ankita Gupta, have been sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder.However, the convictions did not end demands for an investigation into the alleged VIP angle. The registration of an FIR against an unidentified VIP in January 2026 brought renewed attention to the case.Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim governor has now prompted Ankita’s parents to take their demand to India Gate, urging the President to halt the appointment until the CBI investigation is concluded.
Article Summary: Dushyant Kumar Gautam was appointed Sikkim governor on Monday. Ankita Bhandari's family have named him as the alleged VIP in the case. Her parents are protesting at India Gate in Delhi, demanding that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) completes its probe.

They confront the police—and let’s not forget, police personnel are human beings too; they have families," Paswan added.He said escalation by either protesters or the administration was inappropriate, stressing that the use of force could not be justified merely by provocation."This kind of escalation shouldn't happen on either side," he said. "

Article Title: Tibetan parliament calls China's Ladakh claims 'baseless', urges India to scrap One-China policy
Article Text:

India rejects China’s objections over Ladakh

The Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile has criticised China’s refusal to recognise Ladakh as a Union Territory of India, calling Beijing’s territorial claims baseless. It also urged New Delhi to reconsider its Tibet policy amid continuing tensions along the India-China border.The remarks come amid a diplomatic exchange between New Delhi and Beijing over India’s decision to standardise the names of 28 geographical locations and features in Ladakh on official maps, prompting China to reiterate its objections to India’s territorial claims.According to news agency ANI, Dolma Tsering, speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, said China’s attempts to rename geographical locations in Tibet and build villages along border areas were developments India should take seriously in its diplomatic engagement with Beijing.“Beijing’s repeated attempts to rename geographical locations in Tibet and its construction of villages along border areas were concerning developments that India should take seriously while engaging diplomatically with China,” she said.Tsering also cautioned against allowing economic engagement to take precedence over security concerns, saying, “India should not allow trade and business engagements to take precedence over border security, stressing that both issues must be addressed together.”She argued that China’s territorial claims required historical evidence and maintained that Tibet remained central to the unresolved boundary dispute. “A lasting resolution to the border dispute would be difficult without addressing the Tibet issue,” she said.Tsering further alleged that China’s policies promoting ethnic assimilation and prioritising Mandarin over Tibetan threatened Tibet’s distinct cultural and religious identity.She reiterated that the Tibetan leadership’s Middle Way Approach sought a negotiated settlement that would allow Tibetans to preserve their culture, identity and faith, and urged Beijing to resume dialogue.Tibetan MP Gompo Dhondup also rejected China’s claims over Ladakh and other Himalayan regions, including Arunachal Pradesh, asserting that these territories were integral to India and that Beijing had no right to interfere in India’s sovereignty.Dhondup argued that a free and independent Tibet could serve as a peaceful buffer between India and China along their more than 3,000-kilometre border. He called on New Delhi to reconsider its position on Tibet and repeal its One-China policy, saying stronger support for Tibet would serve both Tibetan aspirations and India’s security interests.The latest remarks follow India’s response to Beijing’s objections to the naming exercise. On Tuesday, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated India’s position that Ladakh was an integral part of the country.“It is reiterated that the UT of Ladakh is an integral and inalienable part of India. No amount of denial by the Chinese side can change this established fact,” Jaiswal said.The exchange followed a notification by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) standardising names for 28 locations and geographical features in Ladakh on official Survey of India maps, including Gogra and Hot Spring, sites associated with the 2020 military standoff.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning opposed the move, saying Beijing had never recognised the territory as Indian. “The move is illegal and invalid and cannot change the fact that the relevant areas in the western sector of the China-India boundary have always belonged to China,” she said.
Article Summary: The Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile has criticised China’s refusal to recognise Ladakh as a Union Territory of India. It also urged New Delhi to reconsider its Tibet policy amid continuing tensions along the India-China border. The remarks come amid a diplomatic exchange between New Delhi and Beijing over the names of 28 geographical locations in Ladakh.

Article Title: Govt renames flagship social assistance scheme, drops Indira Gandhi tag
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday approved the continuation of its flagship social security scheme National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for five years until 2031, while renaming it Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana and dropping former PM Indira Gandhi’s name from three of its sub-schemes.Announcing the decision, I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the “comprehensive social security net” will cover vulnerable groups, including the elderly, widows and persons with disabilities. The scheme with an outlay of Rs 53,428 crore is expected to benefit 3.2 crore people.The revamped programme revises the eligibility criteria for pension for persons with disability (PwD) and increases the assistance provided under the sub-scheme.As per the official release, Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme has been renamed PM Vridhavastha Pension Yojana, the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme is now PM Vidhawa Pension Yojana and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme becomes PM Divyangjan Pension Yojana.This comes after the Cabinet approved a new rural employment guarantee scheme, Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), in December last year, replacing the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).Under the revised disability pension sub-scheme, monthly assistance will increase to Rs 375 for beneficiaries from birth to 79 years and to Rs 625 for those aged 80 and above. Till now, beneficiaries aged 18–79 received Rs 300 per month, while those aged 80 and above received Rs 500.The eligibility threshold for benchmark disability has also been reduced to 40% from 80%, bringing the scheme in line with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Govt said the revision was necessitated by the law, which has also mandated that disability-related assistance be at least 25% higher than that provided under comparable schemes for other categories. The revised scheme is expected to cover more than 27.48 lakh beneficiaries.The pension amounts under the old-age and widow pension schemes, as well as assistance under the National Family Benefit Scheme, will remain unchanged. The old-age pension ranges from Rs 200 to Rs 500 per month and covers 221.31 lakh beneficiaries, while the widow pension ranges from Rs 300 to Rs 500 per month and covers 67.38 lakh beneficiaries.Under the National Family Benefit Scheme, a one-time financial assistance of Rs 20,000 is provided to a household following the death of its primary breadwinner, provided the deceased was aged between 18 and 59 years. The scheme covers up to 3.59 lakh beneficiaries.
Article Summary: The Centre on Wednesday approved the continuation of its flagship social security scheme National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for five years until 2031. The revamped programme revises the eligibility criteria for pension for persons with disability (PwD) The scheme with an outlay of Rs 53,428 crore is expected to benefit 3.2 crore people.

Article Title: The Harvard divide over Delhi protests: One group condemns police action, another questions claims of 'siege'
Article Text:

October 12 statement condemns police action

NEW DELHI: The crackdown on protesters in Delhi has triggered a sharp divide among members of the Harvard University community, with two groups issuing contrasting statements, one condemning alleged police excesses and the other cautioning against what it described as a campaign to undermine India's constitutional institutions.Disapproving the use of terms such as “siege” to describe the police deployment in Delhi and “thieves” or “compromised” to characterise constitutional authorities, a section of Harvard affiliates said such language raised concerns about attempts to undermine public trust in democratic institutions."Troubling are reports of the use of Harvard University’s name to lend credibility to a political campaign without appropriate authorisation. The language used to describe India as being under 'siege' and to characterise constitutional authorities as 'thieves' or 'compromised' raises serious concerns about the intent to undermine public trust in democratic institutions," the wider cross-section of the Harvard community, including lawyers, policymakers, civil servants, scientists and academicians, said in a statement.The latest statement signed by 44 individuals raised concerns over what it described as a “concerted campaign” against the country's constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission, the Supreme Court, the office of the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and Parliament."We are deeply concerned by the negative public discourse and concerted campaign against India’s constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission of India , the Supreme Court, the office of the Hon’ble Chief Justice of India, and Parliament," the statement released on Wednesday said.It also addressed the role of law enforcement agencies in maintaining public order, saying their actions should be subject to fair scrutiny but that allegations must be grounded in evidence and due process.“The actions of law enforcement agencies to uphold public order deserve fair scrutiny, but sweeping accusations and abusive rhetoric cannot substitute for evidence, due process or institutional accountability,” the signatories said.They also stressed the need to respect public officials and the offices they hold, adding that constitutional principles and civil liberties must not be applied selectively.“The Constitution, rule of law, and civil liberties must be respected at all times, not just when it suits our interests,” the statement said.Summing up their appeal, the signatories said: “Our commitment must remain to the Constitution, not convenience; to justice, not selective outrage; and to democratic institutions, not the politics of accusation.”In a statement dated October 12, around 100 Harvard alumni, students, faculty and staff condemned what they described as the “unprecedented siege of Delhi by police and paramilitary forces” and alleged arbitrary, illegal and unconstitutional action against peaceful protesters across the country on October 10."We, as alumni, students, faculty, and staff of Harvard University, are deeply concerned by the unprecedented siege of Delhi by police and paramilitary forces and arbitrary, illegal, and unconstitutional police actions against peaceful protestors across the country on 10th October 2026. We strongly condemn police brutality, unlawful detention, and violations of constitutional rights of all peaceful protestors," the letter shared by Live Law read.The signatories condemned alleged police brutality, unlawful detention and violations of protesters' constitutional rights, while expressing solidarity with fellow Harvard affiliates Shadan Farasat, a senior advocate in the Supreme Court and Harvard Law School alumnus from 2009, and Mehr Pasricha, a Harvard Kennedy School graduate from 2025.The signatories called on the government and law enforcement authorities to end alleged violations of constitutional rights, respect the right to peaceful protest and access to legal assistance, and ensure that those responsible for abuses are held accountable under the rule of law.
Article Summary: Harvard-affiliated Indians flag attacks on constitutional institutions and alleged misuse of the university’s name. ‘Our commitment must remain to the Constitution, not convenience; to justice, not selective outrage; and to democratic institutions, not the politics of accusation’

Article Title: SC upholds HC order denying OBC reservation benefits to Hindu converts to Islam
Article Text:
Converts to Islam from Hinduism cannot claim OBC reservation, rules Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a Madras high court ruling that a person who converts to Islam from Hinduism cannot claim reservation benefits under the Backward Class (BC) category.A bench of Justices PK Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar observed that a person who moves from the Hindu social order to a non-Hindu social order cannot claim such benefits.The Tamil Nadu government had challenged the Madras high court order before the Supreme Court.The high court had quashed the state government’s decision to recognise seven Muslim sects as Backward Classes, a move that allowed people from Hindu Backward Classes to be treated as Backward Class Muslims after converting to Islam.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that a person who converts to Islam from Hinduism cannot claim reservation benefits under the Backward Class (BC) category. NEW DELHI: India has asked the UN human rights body when it would issue a report seeking answers from Pakistan on steps taken to address concerns over the situation in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), including investigations into killings and restrictions on internet access.First Secretary at the Permanent Mission of India, Anuj Swarup, delivered the statement during an interactive dialogue with the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee on Wednesday.“When can we expect OHCHR to issue a report on the steps taken by the Government of Pakistan on this? Pakistan would do well to look inwards and reflect on how such rights are not being enjoyed in its large part, including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and for that matter, in Rawalakot, which is under its illegal occupation,” Swarup said.Swarup referred to detailed statements by the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) and the High Commissioner on the situation in PoK. The statements called for prompt, thorough and impartial investigations into killings allegedly carried out by armed and security forces.They also urged authorities to ensure that detained leaders of the Joint Awami Action Committee had access to legal representation and their families, and were afforded due process and a fair trial.The statements further called for lifting internet restrictions across Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir and holding meaningful political dialogue to address the grievances of the local population.The High Commissioner had also noted that dozens of people, mostly protesters but also law enforcement personnel, had reportedly been killed since June, ahead of the July 27 Legislative Assembly elections. Swarup said the OHCHR had adopted an approach of “extreme selectivity” in addressing such incidents.“Violent responses to protests in our neighbourhood as well as in the west have gone uncommented. Needless to say, such double standards contribute to loss of trust in multilateralism and the work of OHCHR,” he said.Swarup said India’s freedom movement, led by Mahatma Gandhi, championed non-violence and equality, values that also shaped the Constitution, which guarantees fundamental rights to every citizen.“Indian citizens exercise rights subject to maintenance of public order and safety. Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available for redressal of any grievance,” he said.Swarup said India, as a member of the UN Human Rights Council, had contributed constructively to discussions on contemporary issues and would continue to engage with the High Commissioner and OHCHR in a “spirit of trust and partnership without selectivity and double standards”.He also stressed that the Indian Constitution guarantees people in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh the same fundamental rights as citizens in other parts of the country, adding that both regions are integral and inalienable parts of India.India’s remarks came days after New Delhi described comments by the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights on protests in the national capital as “unwarranted” and “unacceptable interference” in the country’s internal affairs.Last week, the UN Human Rights Office expressed concern over “reports of mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists, before and during today’s large-scale demonstrations in Delhi.”In a statement, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said, "India is the world’s largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by our Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media."“As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to the maintenance of public order and safety. Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for the redressal of any grievances,” the ministry said.The MEA also accused the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) of selectivity in its public statements, alleging that it had remained silent on violent responses to protests in neighbouring countries and law enforcement actions closer to its own headquarters.
Article Summary: India has asked the UN human rights body when it would issue a report seeking answers from Pakistan on the situation in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. India's first secretary at the Permanent Mission of India, Anuj Swarup, delivered the statement during an interactive dialogue with the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

Article Title: No cancellation of services, cut in metro train trips on October 10, SC told
Article Text:
Delhi Metro Rail Corporation announced the reopening of all metro stations after imposing temporary restrictions.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Wednesday informed Supreme Court that there was no curtailment or cancellation of metro services and no reduction in the number of train trips, with 272 trains operating on Oct 10.“A full complement of 4,157 train trips were conducted on Oct 10 as per schedule across the Metro network,” it said, adding that 258 stations, or 85% of the total number of stations, remained fully operational, accessible and functional for commuters.Following the Supreme Court’s Oct 9 order, which disapproved of a complete shutdown of metro services, Delhi Police reviewed its Oct 8 order for entry/exit closure of 57 of 303 metro stations in Delhi on Oct 10, the day of CJP protest, and applied its directive to 45 stations, DMRC said. It said metro services functioned normally except for closure of entry/exit points at 45 stations on Oct 10 and a total of 32 lakh commuters travelled on the network that day, as against approximately 58 lakh on a normal second Saturday.“Crucially, out of the 45 stations where entry/exit gates were regulated, 14 key interchange stations (including major transit hubs such as Rajiv Chowk, Kashmere Gate, Central Secretariat, Mandi House, Hauz Khas, Dilli Haat-INA and Netaji Subhash Place) continued to provide full and uninterrupted line-interchange facilities for commuters,” it said, adding that all stations were fully operational after 10 pm on Oct 10.“At key sensitive stations, such as GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya, DMRC did not impose a total prohibition on movement; rather, it implemented a measured and calibrated regulatory protocol to control incoming passenger flow while actively facilitating disembarking commuters,” it said.On instructions from police, entry/exit to six metro stations—Patel Chowk, Janpath, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Central Secretariat and Barakhamba Road—were closed from 6 am to 5 pm on Oct 12 to avoid untoward incidents as the police had said there was “likelihood of unruly mob movement towards sensitive locations”, DMRC said.In its Oct 9 order, SC had said, “We clarify that although there shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of metro trains, a prudent decision may be made to permit the operation of Metro trains and other rail services in a suitable and regulated manner.”
Article Summary: Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) informed Supreme Court that there was no curtailment or cancellation of metro services and no reduction in the number of train trips. DMRC said metro services functioned normally except for closure of entry/exit points at 45 stations on Oct 10. 32 lakh commuters travelled on the network that day, as against approximately 58 lakh on a normal second Saturday.

Article Title: SC: Cops can’t seek digital footprints for roving probe
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: SC has said police cannot direct social media platforms under IT Act to share an accused’s digital footprints for periods well before the crime he is being probed for, in an order that is likely to become a precedent for protection of privacy, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.“Information and Technology Act provisions cannot be misused by police to launch a roving and fishing inquiry by obtaining personal data of an accused in breach of right to privacy,” said SC quashing a Ghaziabad Police order asking ‘X’ to furnish digital footprints of journalist Abhishek Upadhyay since June 1 when he was accused of a road rage incident in Aug 18.Cops must apply principles of proportionality, says SCA bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said: “Police must apply the prin-ciples of proportionality while taking steps to investigate a crime and can resort to seeking digital footprints only after recording that alternative methods to obtain information about a crime has proved inadequate”. The court also kept in operation its interim order pro-tecting the journalist from arrest as long as he cooperated with the investigators.Upadhyay, through senior advocate Pradeep Rai, said he had carried out a journalistic investigation into theft of donations at Ayodhya Ram Temple and was first to publish a news article on his digital platform on June 7. The real intent behind the cooked-up FIR of Aug 18 was to seek information from June 1 to identify the sources who informed him about pilferage of donations by devotees, Rai argued.Ghaziabad Police commissioner had informed the court that police searched for the petitioner for three days in connection with the road rage case, in which he is accused of hurling caste slurs at the complainant bike rider, and when he was untraceable, police sought details of digital footprint from ‘X’.SC said the commissioner’s explanation and the order seeking digital footprint details appear to be at variance for the purpose of investigation of the road rage case.“Police can surely look for digital footprints if the crime was committed with long planning and conspiracy, but not in such cases where questions of privacy and right to act as a journalist are involved,” said the bench.Rai with advocate Anoop P Awasthi complained to the court that the journalist’s vehicle, which was seized after the FIR against him, has not been returned. The bench directed Ghaziabad Police to return the vehicle to the petitioner within two days.The bench cautioned Ghaziabad Police against using any of the private and personal information related to the petitioner it has obtained from ‘X’.
Article Summary: SC quashes Ghaziabad Police order asking ‘X’ to furnish digital footprints of journalist Abhishek Upadhyay since June 1 when he was accused of a road rage incident in Aug 18. “Information and Technology Act provisions cannot be misused by police to launch a roving and fishing inquiry by obtaining personal data of an accused in breach of right to privacy,” said SC.

Article Title: SC: Tough PMLA bail conditions can't override accused's right
Article Text:
PMLA accused can't be in jail till trial ends, says SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: SC has said that stringent bail conditions set under special laws such as PMLA cannot override rights granted by the Constitution, holding prolonged incarceration of an undertrial violates the fundamental right to speedy trial.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said an accused could not be kept in custody till completion of trial and held that the accused was entitled to bail in case of delay in trial despite the stringent bail conditions under the anti-money laundering law.Section 45 of PMLA prescribes twin conditions for grant of bail.The PMLA section says no accused shall be released on bail unless the public prosecutor has been given an opportunity to oppose the application for such release, and the court is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing that he is not guilty of such offence and that he is not likely to commit any offence while on bail. The second condition puts the onus on an accused to convince the court that he is not guilty.The bench, however, said, "The twin conditions under Section 45 of PMLA cannot override the constitutional safeguards under Article 21 of the Constitution, as has been held in the case of Manish Sisodia vs Directorate of Enforcement. Prolonged incarceration, if allowed to continue, will set at naught the constitutional safeguards extended to accused persons."The court granted bail to an accused who was allegedly involved in money laundering of over Rs 6,210 crore. ED said the accused had created 62 shell companies, 34 people were made dummy directors and 20 companies were manned by his relatives who contributed to the offence. He was arrested in Dec 2024.Granting him relief, the bench said, "We are of the opinion that the culmination of the trial is a time-consuming process, since the trial court will have to go through documents running into thousands of pages and examine around 98 witnesses. The appellant must not be subjected to the rigours of custody as long as the trial is pending. Hence, the appellant must be released on bail, subject to furnishing of bail bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court and subject to such other terms and conditions as may be imposed by it. "The bench admitted that economic offences were very serious as they impacted the financial fabric of the country but said the rights of accused too have to be protected."In a bail matter, especially in serious offences, the job of a court is to balance the rights of the state with those of the arrestee. In special laws such as PMLA, the conditions for granting bail are stringent, and the circumstances in which bail can be granted are rare, for the simple reason that economic offences of a large magnitude punch a hole through the financial fabric of the country, causing a top-down ripple effect into the entire ecosystem, resulting in large consequences for most of the population.That is the justification for making the provisions of PMLA stringent. In the same breath, sight must not be lost of the fact that the institutions have a duty to expeditiously investigate the cases. Process must not be turned into a punishment unto itself," the court said.The bench referred to its earlier verdict in the Manish Sisodia case in which it was held that prolonged incarceration before being pronounced guilty of an offence should not be permitted to become punishment without trial, and keeping the appellant behind bars for an unlimited period of time in the hope of speedy completion of trial would deprive him of his fundamental right to liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution.
Article Summary: Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said an accused could not be kept in custody till completion of trial. The accused was entitled to bail in case of delay in trial despite the stringent bail conditions under the anti-money laundering law.

Article Title: India to Starlink: Comply with rules before entering market
Article Text:
