Mittal: Ahead of Musk in queue for approval

NEW DELHI: Starlink is yet to receive clearance to launch services in India as it has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to set up domestic infrastructure, a senior govt official said Wednesday, sending a tough message to tech trillionaire Elon Musk that in order to do business in India he will have to abide by the law of the land.Govt has no objection to the satellite internet provider rolling out its services once it addresses security concerns and agrees to establish local base stations before it can offer services in India, sources said. A base station is a radio transmitter and receiver that acts as a local hub, or the "first hop", connecting end-user devices to a wireless network. The requirement to set up "base stations" will help authorities to secure compliance with laws.Sunil Bharti Mittal-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio and Musk's Starlink are the three entities planning to start satellite communication services in India.Significantly, another message to Musk that he cannot expect to be an exception to the law came from Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal, who said Airtel's Eutelsat OneWeb satellite service might receive regulatory approvals ahead of Starlink, as it is "way ahead" in the approval queue, having applied nearly five years ago.He added that he will be "very happy" to get it at least a few days before Starlink.Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal on Tuesday said his company deserved to get approval to start a satellite internet service before Elon Musk’s Starlink as Airtel’s Eutelsat OneWeb had submitted its application earlier.“I am significantly ahead in the queue from him. I applied five years back. I have my ground networks ready for three years. My satellites have been hovering over India for last five years... We will be happy to get it at least a few days before him,” said Mittal at Bloomberg New Economy Forum, in response to a query soliciting his views on Musk’s recent tirade, as he accused Indian telecom providers of preventing Starlink from entering the Indian market.Govt has denied Musk’s charge that Starlink was being discriminated against at the instance of a “local oligarch”.
Article Summary: Starlink has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to set up domestic infrastructure, a senior govt official said. Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Mittal said Airtel's Eutelsat OneWeb might receive regulatory approvals ahead of Starlink, as it is "way ahead" in the approval queue.

NEW DELHI: India and Canada reviewed progress in their ties across trade and investment, education, energy, defence and people-to-people exchanges as Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand called on Prime Minister Narendra Modi Wednesday and also held a meeting with her counterpart S Jaishankar.Modi emphasised the importance of sustaining the momentum in bilateral engagement and translating it into tangible outcomes, including through the early conclusion of negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), and said he was looking forward to continuing his engagements with Canadian PM Mark Carney."India is committed to building a constructive and forward-looking strategic partnership with Canada that delivers tangible benefits to the people of both countries," Modi said in a post on X, calling the meeting productive.Modi is set to visit Canada in Dec during which both sides are expected to sign the CEPA under discussion.In the meeting with Jaishankar, Anand highlighted the importance that Canada attaches to India as a partner, particularly at a time of geopolitical uncertainty."Minister Anand and minister Jaishankar discussed the positive momentum in the renewed Canada-India Strategic Partnership, underpinned by sustained high-level engagement between the two countries over the last year," said a Canadian readout.The ministers also reviewed progress made since the launch of the joint roadmap during Anand's visit last year and discussed ways to further advance roadmap priorities, including trade, energy, people-to-people ties and security and defence cooperation. The ministers discussed other geopolitical issues, including the West Asia conflict and the war in Ukraine, the Canadian readout said.The ministers welcomed the recent security dialogue held in India at the NSA level, where officials reviewed progress in bilateral security and law enforcement cooperation and committed to sustained engagement on security issues of mutual interest."The ministers also welcomed efforts to advance negotiations for a comprehensive economic partnership agreement," the readout further said.
Article Summary: India and Canada reviewed progress in their ties across trade and investment, education, energy, defence and people-to-people exchanges. Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand called on Prime Minister Narendra Modi Wednesday. Anand also held a meeting with her counterpart S Jaishankar.
